content: Valacyclovir has several important warnings and precautions that must be considered when prescribing or administering the medication: 1. Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura/Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (TTP/HUS): Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura and hemolytic uremic syndrome (TTP/HUS) have been reported in patients taking valacyclovir, particularly in those with advanced HIV-1 disease, as well as in recipients of allogeneic bone marrow transplants and renal transplants. These conditions can be life-threatening and have, in some cases, resulted in death. If a patient develops clinical signs, symptoms, or laboratory findings consistent with TTP/HUS, treatment with valacyclovir must be discontinued immediately. 2. Acute Renal Failure: Cases of acute renal failure have been observed in several patient populations: Elderly patients: Older adults, regardless of whether they have reduced renal function, are at increased risk. Careful monitoring is required, and dose adjustments are recommended for those with impaired renal function. Patients with pre-existing renal disease: Those with underlying kidney conditions who receive doses of valacyclovir higher than recommended for their level of renal function are at risk. Dosage reductions are necessary in these cases. Patients taking nephrotoxic drugs: Caution is advised when valacyclovir is administered alongside other medications that may harm the kidneys. Patients with inadequate hydration: Insufficient hydration can lead to the precipitation of acyclovir in the renal tubules, particularly when its solubility threshold (2.5 mg/mL) is exceeded in the intratubular fluid. To prevent this, patients should maintain adequate hydration. In cases of acute renal failure or anuria (absence of urine production), hemodialysis may be beneficial to restore renal function. 3. Central Nervous System (CNS) Effects: Adverse effects on the central nervous system have been reported in both adult and pediatric patients. These effects include agitation, hallucinations, confusion, delirium, seizures, and encephalopathy. Such reactions have occurred in patients with or without reduced renal function, as well as in those with underlying renal disease who received doses of valacyclovir higher than recommended for their renal function. Elderly patients are particularly susceptible to CNS side effects. If any CNS adverse reactions occur, valacyclovir should be discontinued immediately.
